title: add-fragment-sequencer-json-rollup-and-ordered-toolcall-handoff
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: In high-concurrency streaming scenarios we observed rare but customer-visible cases where SSE fragments that split JSON payloads or function-call sentinels could be reordered by upstream buffering layers, resulting in malformed partial JSON or tool/function-call ordering anomalies. This PR introduces a fragment sequencer and a conservative JSON rollup guard to make streaming reconstruction deterministic and resilient to reordering, partial-deliveries, and delimiter corruption.

What this changes: Adds a lightweight per-stream fragment sequencer that stamps outbound SSE fragments with a monotonic fragment_seq and epoch header (SSE-Seq-Version:2). The server-side assembler uses the sequencer to: 1) reorder late-arriving fragments within a bounded window; 2) detect missing fragments and trigger a rollup-rescue path instead of emitting a partial JSON event; 3) normalize and collapse duplicate trailing delimiters before handing events to the structured-output pipeline. To preserve strict function/tool-call ordering we also attach an ordered-toolcall-ordinal to fncall sentinel frames so downstream tool invocations see a deterministic ordinal even under retransmit/replay.

Design notes: Sequencer is intentionally small: fragments carry probe metadata (frag_seq, epoch, frag_len). The assembler keeps a bounded reorder buffer (configurable via sse.max_reseq_window) and exposes two outcomes: ASSEMBLED (complete, in-order) and ROLLUP (best-effort rescue that concatenates fragments, validates JSON, and emits a trimmed structured event plus diagnostics). The rollup guard performs UTF-8 safety checks, trailing comma fixes for common serializer truncations, and adds a metadata field sse.rollup_hint to downstream structured-output events for traceability.

Compatibility: The change is backward-compatible for clients that ignore SSE-Seq-Version headers; existing plain-fragment flows remain supported. New behavior is opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers via a runtime flag (sse.enable_sequencer) during initial rollout; hosted API will enable rollouts progressively after Canary.

Testing: Unit tests for sequencer edge cases, fuzz tests for mid-json truncation, and integration tests that simulate interleaved fragments, delayed retransmits, and toolcall replays were added. Load tests show sequencing adds <1% p99 latency at typical token sizes and reduces partial-JSON error rate by ~98% in synthetic reorder workloads. New metrics: sse.fragment_reseqs, sse.rollup_rescues, sse.toolcall_ord_mismatches.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary region with sse.enable_sequencer=false by default and run synthetic repros; 2) Enable sequencing for 5% of traffic with auto-fallback to previous emitter if rollup_rescues exceed threshold; 3) Gradual ramp and post-deploy monitoring via new dashboards.

Notes for reviewers: Look at the reassembly invariants in pkg/stream/sse/sequencer.go and the rescue heuristics in pkg/stream/sse/rollup_guard.go. The change includes small API surface additions to the streaming handshake header only (no public SDK breaking changes).

review_comments: Jun Park: 'Can you explain the choice of window size and how it affects memory under pathological reordering?' — Aisha: 'Default window is 64 fragments, we've observed it's sufficient for typical network reorder; made it configurable to 256 for extreme tests and added backpressure to drop oldest entries with metrics.'; Lina Gomez: 'Need clearer signal on when rollup_rescue happens for customer debugging' — Aisha: 'Added sse.rollup_hint and structured diagnostic payloads; updated docs with examples.'; Tomás Rivera: 'Race in reorder buffer removal noted in initial run' — Aisha: 'Fixed in a0b1c2d, added a deterministic integration test.'; Approval: Lina and Tomás approved after fixes; Jun gave LGTM after CI rerun.
release_notes: Add fragment sequencing and JSON rollup guards to improve SSE streaming resilience: reduces partial-JSON emissions, preserves tool/function-call ordering, adds sse.fragment_reseqs and sse.rollup_rescues metrics. Opt-in via sse.enable_sequencer; rollout will be gradual.
qa_notes: Run scripts/loadtests/sse_reorder_workload.yaml against canary; verify sse.rollup_rescues metric is near-zero under normal networks and dominates only during forced reorder tests.
performance_impact: observed <1% p99 latency increase in our lab at default settings; configurable window to tune tradeoff
notes_for_ops: Add monitors for sse.fragment_reseqs and sse.rollup_rescues; add alert if rollup_rescues > 0.5% of stream events during rollout
